course_name_original: Criptografía y Codificación de la Información
prerequisites: Notions of algorithm design and analysis

learning_outcomes.text: Know the computer security techniques that allow maintaining privacy, confidentiality and integrity in access to data and knowledge, including basic cryptography concepts.
Understand the language and interpret concepts and parameters involved in Cryptography and Coding.
Understand the objectives of Error Correcting Codes Theory and Cryptography.
Recognize the presence and importance of error correcting codes and cipher systems in solving real-life digital security problems.
Identify different families and classical code constructions and build error correcting codes with specific parameters.
Manipulate encryption systems, both public and private key, and recognize situations for using some cryptosystems over others, as well as other cryptographic protocols.
Handle symbolic calculation programs for manipulating the elements involved in Code Theory and Cryptography.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical foundations of Cryptography and Coding.
Introduction to codes. Linear codes. Cyclic codes. Other error correcting codes.
Introduction to cryptography. Private key cryptography. Public key cryptography and digital signatures. Other cryptographic protocols.
Introduction to error detecting and correcting codes.
Linear codes. Generator and parity-check matrix. Code parameters.
Cyclic codes: Reed-Solomon and BCH codes.
Other codes. Real applications of Code Theory.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance / Participation in Seminars and Tutorials (including online)
Active Participation in Virtual Campus Forums and Activities

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) in the ordinary examination will be calculated as NF = 0.05 NA + 0.2 NC + 0.5 NP + 0.25 NT, where NA is the attendance/participation grade, NC is the participation grade, NP is the practice grade, and NT is the objective test grade. All grades are out of 10 points. The course is passed if NF ≥ 5. For students with officially recognized differentiated evaluation and in extraordinary examinations, the subject will be evaluated by a single final theoretical-practical objective test with a weight of 100%.
